text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High CrashLoopBackOff rate for deployment response-processor (canary) in eu-west-2 — auto-paged to oncall
Alex: I'm taking the page, looking at events. CrashLoopBackOff + failed liveness.
ops-bot: K8s event stream: FailedKill -> OOMKilled x12, Liveness probe failed x9 on pod response-processor-canary-5b9c. Node eu-w-2-07 under memory pressure.
Ming: deploy-bot shows rollout for response-processor started ~4m ago: image rev v3.1.0-canary, configmap response-config updated (memoryMultiplier=2).
deploy-bot: rollout initiated by Victor (victor@redwood). canary=15%.
Alex: I see the canary manifest has liveness probe failureThreshold=3, periodSeconds=10. New config increases default cache size by memoryMultiplier -> doubles resident set. Not good.
Claire: We also had a scheduled node drain on eu-w-2-07 at 02:02Z for kernel updates. Could be coincidence.
Victor: I pushed a perf tweak to cache sizing to reduce latency; that change was intended for staging. I'm checking why config scoping allowed prod.
Alex: Immediate steps: 1) pause rollout 2) flip route feature flag to send traffic away from canary 3) scale canary to 3 replicas and increase requests/limits to prevent OOM while we rollback 4) uncordon node if safe.
Ming: I'll pause the rollout now.
```
kubectl rollout pause deployment/response-processor -n prod
```
Ming: paused.
Alex: flipping flag to route-v3 -> off
```
ffctl set response-route-v3 false --env=prod
```
Claire: flag set to false. traffic should stop reaching canary. CS: any user-facing alerts?
Victor: CS reported a spike in 502s for EU API clients starting ~02:05Z. They're sending status updates.
Alex: patching hpa/min replicas and pod resources to stabilize while we rollback:
```
kubectl patch hpa response-processor --namespace=prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":2}]'
kubectl set resources deployment/response-processor-canary -n prod --requests=cpu=250m,memory=600Mi --limits=cpu=500m,memory=1Gi
kubectl scale deployment/response-processor-canary --replicas=3 -n prod
```
Ming: HPA patched, resources updated, scaling to 3. New pods are coming up but one still CrashLooping.
ops-bot: Node eu-w-2-07 still has pressure, 1 pod evicted.
Alex: I'm going to uncordon eu-w-2-08 (cordoned earlier by maintenance) so scheduler has more room.
```
kubectl uncordon eu-w-2-08
```
Ming: uncordoned, node becomes Ready. Scheduler rebalances. Memory pressure falling.
Alex: Rolling back canary image to last-known-good v3.0.9 and restarting:
```
kubectl set image deployment/response-processor-canary response-processor=registry.redwood/response-processor:v3.0.9 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/response-processor-canary -n prod
```
Victor: rollback applied; new pods with v3.0.9 starting and passing liveness.
Claire: CS says error rate back to baseline in EU, customers report restored sessions.
Alex: quick RCA notes in thread: root cause chain: 1) non-prod config (memoryMultiplier=2) accidentally promoted due to pipeline config selector bug; 2) scheduled node maintenance reduced capacity at same time; 3) HPA/minReplicas and pod resource defaults allowed pods to be OOMKilled; 4) liveness probe parameters triggered restarts before backoff.
Ming: immediate mitigations we executed: paused rollout, flipped feature flag, patched HPA minReplicas, bumped pod resources, uncordoned node, rolled back image.
Victor: action items (owners):
- Victor: fix pipeline selector so config from staging cannot be promoted to prod by mismatch (owner: Victor)
- Ming: add CI lint rule: disallow minReplicas=0 for prod canaries and require explicit resource requests (owner: Ming)
- Alex: create alert for sustained CrashLoopBackOff rate > 10% across a deployment canary (owner: Alex)
- Claire: update customer-facing timeline and notify top 50 EU customers (owner: Claire)
- Ops: adjust maintenance windows to avoid overlapping active canaries (owner: Ops)
Alex: Customer impact window ~02:04Z-02:18Z; estimated affected API calls ~7.5k requests, elevated latencies for ~6k sessions. Claire, please draft the short status update.
Claire: drafting now; will post to status.redwood.ai by 03:20Z.
Victor: scheduling follow-up postmortem tomorrow 09:00AM PT. Will include archive of canary manifests and pipeline logs.
Ming: handing off to daytime oncall at 07:30Z, I've added notes to the oncall doc.
ops-bot: INCIDENT: mitigations implemented, monitoring for 60m, no regression observed in last 10m.
Alex: closing page, leaving thread pinned for postmortem and action-tracking. :white_check_mark:
